references.text: Here the recipe for the holy anointing oil is given, along with instructions to anoint the tabernacle and all its furnishings to consecrate them.
Aaron and his sons are to be anointed to serve as priests, parallel to the anointing of the tabernacle.
The altar is to be anointed to consecrate it, following the same principle applied to the entire tabernacle.
Moses performs the anointing of the tabernacle and everything in it, sprinkling oil on the altar seven times to consecrate it.
Refers to the day when Moses completed setting up the tabernacle, anointed it, and consecrated it along with all its utensils.
Continues the instructions for anointing the bronze altar of burnt offering and the basin to consecrate them.
The book of Hebrews refers to Moses sprinkling blood on the tabernacle and all the utensils used in worship as part of the consecration.
Describes the actual fulfillment of the command to anoint and consecrate the tabernacle.
Highlights the theological principle that holiness is transferred to everything that touches the holy objects.
Shows the parallel process by which the priests must also be anointed and consecrated in the same way as the tabernacle.
Develops the concept of 'most holy' and confirms that anything that touches the holy things becomes holy.
